name: rein storage backend
definition: rein's storage backend is SQLite with the FTS5 full-text extension and sqlite-vec for 3072-dim cosine vectors. WAL mode plus SQLITE_OPEN_FULL_MUTEX provides per-connection isolation; a per-request connection model avoids a shared mutex on the SqliteStore. The original PostgreSQL prototype was rejected: deployment overhead outweighed the concurrency headroom for a single-user agent workload.

revisions.definition: rein's storage backend is PostgreSQL with pgvector for vector similarity and a standard btree index for keyword lookup. PostgreSQL was chosen for its mature concurrency story and the existing pgvector ecosystem.

rein's storage backend was migrated from PostgreSQL to SQLite with sqlite-vec. Rationale: deployment complexity of PostgreSQL was not justified for a single-user agent; SQLite with WAL mode handles the expected write throughput, and sqlite-vec ships cosine search without a separate server.

name: MergeInto cap handling
definition: The MergeInto cap is 10KB per canonical memory body. When a merge would push the body past the cap, v0.23 dispatches the canonical to the resummerize slow-channel op (gated by the 7-invariant Lossless Compression Contract and feature-flagged off by default). Keep-tail truncation remains the synchronous stopgap: needs_resummerize is flagged alongside keep-tail so the effective body is always well-formed even before the slow channel runs.

revisions.definition: The MergeInto cap is 10KB. When a merge exceeds it, the incoming evidence is appended and the oldest portion of the canonical body is hard-truncated in place. This keep-tail strategy preserves the most recent context at the cost of historical evidence.

The MergeInto cap is 10KB. v0.21 ships keep-tail truncation as the primary strategy. An LLM-driven alternative (resummerize) is under design but not yet implemented; keep-tail remains the production path.
